name: Eliashib
title: High Priest after the Exile
summary: Eliashib was the high priest in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time and played an important role in rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem. He is also known for his controversial family connections with Tobiah the Ammonite and Sanballat the Horonite, which led to conflicts with Nehemiah.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding of the Sheep Gate
keyEvents.description: Eliashib led the priests in rebuilding the Sheep Gate in Jerusalem's wall, and they consecrated it and set up its doors.

keyEvents.title: Connection with Tobiah
keyEvents.description: Eliashib had a close connection with Tobiah the Ammonite and even arranged a large room in the temple courts for him, which was a serious breach of the sanctuary's purity.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah Cleanses the Temple Courts
keyEvents.description: When Nehemiah returned to Jerusalem, he threw Tobiah's belongings out of the room that Eliashib had made available and cleansed the rooms.

keyEvents.title: Family Connection with Sanballat
keyEvents.description: One of Eliashib's sons, Joiada, had a son who was a son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, which caused Nehemiah to drive him away.

keyEvents.title: Recorded in the Genealogy of the Priests
keyEvents.description: Eliashib is mentioned in the genealogy of the high priests as the son of Joiakim and father of Joiada, placing him in the line of high priestly succession after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Priestly Service under Eliashib
keyEvents.description: In the book of Nehemiah, the heads of families among the priests who served during Eliashib's time as high priest are mentioned, and their names were recorded in the chronicles.
